title: Artificial Intelligence as a Pedagogical Tool in Lesson Planning: Implications for Self-Confidence and Professional Development of Physical Education Student Teachers
extended_summary:
This study examines whether artificial intelligence can support lesson planning for physical education student teachers and whether that support is associated with stronger self-confidence and professional development. The paper is motivated by the idea that lesson planning is a demanding part of teacher preparation, especially during internship periods when student teachers must translate theory into practice while managing organization, decision-making, and instructional uncertainty.

The intervention/approach studied is AI-assisted lesson planning, framed as a pedagogical scaffold rather than a replacement for professional judgment. The authors used a mixed-methods design combining a questionnaire with open-ended responses, focusing on perceptions of AI use for planning efficiency, organization of content, pedagogical differentiation, time management, and teaching-method diversification, as well as confidence, stress, competence, and professional growth. The sample consisted of 100 physical education student teachers at the Higher Institute of Sport and Physical Education in Tunis, Tunisia, all participating in supervised internship teaching.

Findings were generally positive: participants reported that AI helped them plan more efficiently, organize content, and feel more confident, with significant correlations between AI-supported planning and several confidence/professional-development measures. The strongest associations were observed for organization of educational content, pedagogical decision-making, and perceived professional development. At the same time, the study notes that AI did not eliminate stress entirely and that digital competence, ethical use, and pedagogical guidance remain important constraints. Overall, the paper concludes that AI can enhance planning quality and confidence in teacher preparation when implemented ethically and with adequate support.

identified_tools.name: GenAI (General)
identified_tools.description: A general generative AI/LLM tool used to support lesson planning by generating ideas, structured guidance, and feedback, without a specific commercial product named in the paper.
identified_tools.use_case: Used by physical education student teachers during internship lesson planning to improve lesson organization, time management, instructional differentiation, and perceived professional confidence.

findings.finding_summary: In a mixed-methods sample of physical education student teachers (n=100), AI-supported lesson planning was associated with better perceived planning quality, efficiency, and organization. Participants reported that AI reduced lesson-preparation time, improved diversification of teaching methods, and was positively related to confidence in pedagogical decision-making and professional development.
findings.measure: Questionnaire ratings on AI use in lesson planning and perceived planning quality/efficiency

findings.finding_summary: AI use was positively associated with self-confidence outcomes. Significant correlations were reported between AI-supported lesson planning and confidence in pedagogical decisions (r=.301, p=.002), confidence using AI tools (r=.380, p<.001), and professional development (e.g., r=.457 for educational content organization with professional development), although stress reduction was weaker and not always significant.
findings.measure: Questionnaire ratings on teacher self-confidence, stress, and professional development

findings.finding_summary: Participants generally agreed that AI improved planning efficiency and reduced the time needed to prepare lessons. For example, 73% agreed or strongly agreed that AI reduces planning time, and 63% agreed that it helps them plan more efficiently. Correlations also showed that efficient planning using AI was significantly related to higher confidence and professional development (e.g., r=.415, p<.001 for professional development).
findings.measure: Likert-scale items on time management and planning efficiency

findings.finding_summary: The paper argues that AI-supported lesson planning can strengthen professional identity formation during teacher training, but implementation requires ethical safeguards and guided use. It also notes variability in experiences due to digital competence and cautions that AI should support, not replace, human judgment.
findings.measure: Qualitative thematic analysis of open-ended responses and discussion of ethical use

quality_tier_rationale: This is a mixed-methods correlational study with qualitative themes, not an experimental design. It provides useful empirical evidence but cannot establish causal effects of AI on planning quality or instructional practice.
impact_tier_rationale: The reported associations are mostly modest-to-moderate, with several correlations at or above r=.30 and some as high as r=.554. The strongest effects suggest meaningful practical relevance for planning quality and self-confidence, though stress reduction is weaker and the tool is not specifically named.
